newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tankers bouyed by ULCC interest.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tankers bouyed by ULCC interest.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering activity was healthy in some sectors on Tuesday and brokers saw interest for large tonnages, but most rates for smaller ships were unchanged.

Middle Eastern markets were buoyed by chartering interest for at least three ULCCs and one broker said Vela had fixed at least one for the Red Sea or further west. KPC was also heard looking for 3-400,000 tonnes' worth of carriage.
Brokers assessed rates for VLCCs at around W57.5 to Japan, and a few points less to other Asian destinations. Mideast/Europe was pegged at about W52.5.

While VLCCs found good business in West Africa, with three fixed for South Africa, China and the U.S. Gulf, West African Suezmax markets were also strong, with a W97.5 seen fixed for a 135,000 tonner fixed from West Africa to the U.S. Atlantic coast.

But a disappointing W87.5 was paid by BP for a 120,000 tonne Suezmax to the Mediterranean. One described this as a "blip" in an otherwise healthy market, but another said rates were under pressure from an increasing surplus of tonnage.
Oil tankers sailing across the Med were pegged at around W107.5 for modern 80,000 tonne Aframax ships while older vessels were around 5 points lower.
Activity was limited but dealers saw little room for large price falls. "There is not much demand and it may drop by a few points but it should settle between W100 and W105," a broker said.
UK/Continent rates for Aframaxes were slightly weaker amid a dearth of demand. But little further movement was envisaged. "I see no reason why it should not stay around W100-105," one broker said.
